tasks.title: Freeze contracts and establish the macOS project
tasks.status: implemented
deliverables: Create an arm64 native macOS app and bundled XPC inference target, with fixed bundle IDs and a 26.5.2 runtime floor.
Define versioned capture, transcript, diarization, summary, edit, model-manifest and job contracts from plan section 9.
Specify integer nanosecond session time, UTC display metadata, per-source epochs/frame counters, explicit gap events, and immutable revision IDs.
Add deterministic fixtures for a two-source conversation, overlap, missing source, pause and stale-summary case; include a fake worker.
acceptance: App and worker build in the chosen pinned Xcode/Swift toolchain on supported macOS.
Contract round trips preserve source, overlapping intervals, unknown speakers, null owners and evidence references.
A worker crash is observable without terminating the app; fixture UI state distinguishes captured audio from failed processing.
Document all confirmed user choices and remaining assumptions; dependent agents use these types.

deliverables: Build a release-mode replay harness for separate-source ASR, diarization and summary stages.

tasks.title: Prove arbitrary-application audio capture
tasks.status: implemented (manual app/device matrix pending)
deliverables: Implement nonmuting private Core Audio system tap plus one selected microphone input, with separate source meters.
Use preallocated realtime rings; copy frames/timestamps only in callbacks and write test segments off-thread.
Obtain permissions using public APIs/normal capture prompts with NSMicrophoneUsageDescription and NSAudioCaptureUsageDescription where applicable.
Test app-self audio exclusion, new processes after start, browser playback, different output routes and route changes under the app bundle identity.
Publish a source/device/OS compatibility matrix and an unsupported-format diagnostic rather than silently downscoping capture.
acceptance: On macOS 26.5.2, captured known signals prove mic and system audio both exist and are distinct; first frames reach the writer within 2 seconds after permission and the first segment commits within 4 seconds.
Zoom, Teams, Meet, Slack and generic playback trials use capture without meeting APIs; manual tests identify every tested app version.
Recording does not mute or change the user playback route, and self playback does not recursively enter system capture.
A 30-minute loaded capture has no ring overruns, timing discontinuity without an event, or blocking/allocating callback work.
tasks.fallback: Reduce to a minimal signed tap reproducer. Evaluate ScreenCaptureKit only for a demonstrated tap blocker. Do not use private TCC APIs or require a virtual driver by default.

tasks.title: Make recordings durable and recoverable
tasks.status: implemented
deliverables: Implement two-second CAF segments, atomic publication, journal, checksums, per-minute sharding and SQLite indexing.
Record sample counts, format epochs, session timestamp mappings, explicit pause/sleep/gap/device-change events.
Recover committed files without index rows; quarantine truncated/corrupt files and preserve valid existing segments.
Implement disk projections, reserve margin, safe stop, callback/commit watchdogs, and pinned/default microphone policy.
acceptance: Random force-kill tests recover every committed segment and meet the measured 5-second tail-loss target under the reference load.
Healthy input persists while the other source disconnects; every affected interval is visible.
Two-hour capture does not accumulate PCM in memory; timeline drift remains below 100 ms at known alignment markers after normalization.
Low disk saves a playable partial meeting and does not delete earlier recordings. Callback p99 and memory gates pass.
tasks.fallback: Adjust segment size/durability policy using measured loss and disk latency. Never mark a gap as recorded silence or a failed save as complete.

tasks.title: Orchestrate isolated resumable processing
tasks.status: implemented
deliverables: Implement durable stage DAG, leases/heartbeats, content-addressed idempotent results, retries and cancellation.
Run one heavy stage at a time, with model unload/restart boundaries and bounded XPC payloads.
Suspend heavy work during a new recording and react to thermal/memory pressure; expose queued/paused status.
